beats.lead: The reason your to do list nags you, according to every productivity blog
beats.text: Unfinished tasks are supposed to stick in memory better than finished ones.
beats.note: It is named the Zeigarnik effect, after a 1927 study, and shows up in almost every article about why checklists work.

beats.name: Bluma Zeigarnik
beats.role: Psychologist working with Kurt Lewin. She turned an odd detail, a waiter who forgot every order the moment the bill was paid, into a real experiment.

beats.text: Later attempts to repeat the result kept failing.
beats.note: A 1968 study found no real difference in memory between finished and unfinished tasks.

beats.lead: In 2025, a full review made it official
beats.text: Researchers found no memory advantage for unfinished tasks at all.
beats.note: Their own conclusion: the Zeigarnik effect lacks universal validity.

beats.text: A related effect, the urge to go back and finish something, held up fine. That one just never got the famous name.

beats.line: The habit survived. The reason you were given for it did not.
